title: Verb tense: timeline and consistency
subtitle: Form, Structure, and Sense · 31 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **31 of the official questions in Form, Structure, and Sense are this one** — 26 Easy, 5 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The subject already agrees with every choice, and the choices differ only in tense or aspect: past, present, past perfect ('had ___ed'), future progressive, 'was ___ing'.
- The sentence has other time clues, like dates, 'when/before/after', or verbs in a parallel clause.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Circle the other verbs and time markers in the sentence or the next one.
- 2) If one past event happened before another past event, use 'had + past participle'.
- If the sentence describes a literary work, a general truth, or a parallel clause in the present, match that present tense.
- 3) Otherwise, match the tense that is already set.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Simple past feels natural whenever there is a date, but it loses the before-and-after order that the past perfect shows.
For books and characters, the trap is switching to past tense when the parallel clause uses the literary present.

sections.heading: You are losing these
